case_name: Kanwal Kishore Jerath v Union Territory of Chandigarh
respondent:
Union Territory of Chandigarh
Supreme Court of India

19 March 2001
Petition(s) for Special Leave to Appeal (Cr.) No. 390-393/2001
The order of the Court was as follows:
1.  The petitioner is facing trial before the learned Special Judge, Chandigarh in an offence under section 13 (1) (d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act read with sections 406, 409, 420 and 467 of the IPC. Out of the 51 accused persons facing trial, 50 of them are on bail and petitioner is the only person, who has not been granted bail.
2.  Petitioner had earlier approached this Court, but the Court by order dated 15-12-1999 rejected the prayer at that stage taking into account the gravity of offence. facts: The petitioner is facing trial before the learned Special Judge, Chandigarh in an offence under section 13 (1) (d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act read with sections 406, 409, 420 and 467 of the IPC.
Out of the 51 accused persons facing trial, 50 of them are on bail and petitioner is the only person, who has not been granted bail.
Petitioner had earlier approached this Court, but the Court by order dated 15-12-1999 rejected the prayer at that stage taking into account the gravity of offence.
The High Court by the impugned order examined the materials and came to the conclusion that in the case in hand, the petitioner ought not to be released on bail.
respondent_arguments: Ms.Jaiswal for the Union Territory of Chandigarh
court_reasoning: We think it appropriate to release the petitioner on bail and we accordingly so direct.
We leave the matter open for being pressed before the learned Special Judge, who will consider the submissions made by the Public Prosecutor,
